speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I need to examine your skin lesions to assess for potential malignancy; do you have any new moles, changing spots, or persistent rashes you are concerned about? Please describe their size, color, shape, and how they have evolved over time.

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history; the combination of a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the penis and a similar lesion on your finger is concerning given your smoking history. Have you noticed any bleeding, pain, or ulceration in these areas, and do you have any family history of skin cancer or immune suppression?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Non-healing, crusty, red lesions on the penile shaft and left middle finger. I also have Lesions are painless, History of unsuccessful treatment for syphilis and eczema.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (SCC) of the penis and digit. The clinical presentation of non-healing, crusty, painless lesions in a heavy smoker with a history of failed treatments for syphilis and eczema is highly suggestive of SCC. I request immediate biopsy results for both lesions to confirm the diagnosis.
